endorsements.quote: Standardize calibration methods like Platt or temperature scaling and present Brier scores with calibration plots in model development.
All spatial AI-derived biomarkers should follow the TRIPOD-AI and CLAIM guidelines for predictive model development and validation.

Spatial biomarkers for clinical decision-making should be developed as Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) under the FDA's AI/ML-enabled SaMD framework, with analytical validity established through inter-scanner variability studies, clinical validity in prospective trials, and clinical utility shown through improved patient outcomes or cost-effectiveness.
Hence, the cut-off must be established before the prospective trial begins, no post-hoc optimization.
Next-generation explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) frameworks match model reasoning with pathologist-validated biological features to overcome these constraints.

unlisted_practices: Require raw data, processing pipelines, and analytic code to be shared as a condition of publication.
Pre-register analyses and use standardized, publicly accessible spatial atlases for biomarker development.
Include in prospective clinical evaluation only spatial variables that pass adversarial external validation across institutions, platforms, and demographic strata.
Report negative and failed validation results, and have journals publish them.
Use federated learning to train and validate models across institutions without sharing patient-level images.
Document systematic failure modes filtered by clinically relevant subgroups and evaluate models using net reclassification improvement at pre-specified decision thresholds.
Validate AI-derived biomarkers in biomarker-stratified randomized trials using locked assays with pre-specified cut-offs.
Publish uncertainty intervals around biomarker cut-offs to inform future recalibration.
Funders should mandate replication studies as deliverables.
